records.name: Cagayan Valley
records.summary: On 31 July 2024 in Ilagan City, Isabela, Morine "G." Cabansag, 40, was found dead in a cemetery after an alleged kidnapping and rape in Centro San Antonio; three suspects were identified. The monitored trans-murder count records the cause as stabbing. This is one of six documented killings of trans women in eighteen months in the national series, with arrests made in at least three of them and none reported prosecuted to conviction. No protective ordinance, institutional-hostility finding or enforcement pattern specific to trans visitors is documented in this region beyond this single incident.

records.name: Western Visayas
records.summary:
On 10 October 2022 the Capiz State University Office of Student Affairs told students perceived as trans women that they would be barred from university premises unless they cut their hair and wore the uniform prescribed for males, delivering the instruction through campus guards with one week to comply and threatening that they could not re-enroll otherwise; the office attributed the order to the university president. A legal-NGO case study documents the students' subsequent advocacy campaign — backed by paralegals of national LGBTQ organisations, who pointed to an existing municipal anti-discrimination ordinance in Roxas City, Capiz, which the office dismissed as inapplicable — and its later milestone: the first openly trans woman graduating as university valedictorian with highest honours. This is a documented episode of institutional gender-expression policing in a provincial (not metropolitan) setting, reversed by advocacy.

No killings from the 2024-2025 national series occurred in this region. The campus directive is a resident-facing action rather than a mechanism a visitor encounters; its force as a region signal is that in a conservative provincial setting expression can be policed by institutional authority without an operational local recourse — unlike Central Visayas, this region has no protective ordinance cluster of comparable reach.

records.name: Ilocos Region
records.summary:
The Pangasinan provincial board certified and affirmed Municipal Ordinance No. 15, s-2023 of Bayambang protecting the rights of LGBTQI persons (Provincial Board Resolution No. 799-2024, session of 19 August 2024)—a provincial-level endorsement of a municipal LGBTQ+ protection ordinance in a conservative province. This gives a visitor in the Pangasinan corridor a local complaint route absent in most other regions.

Against that, the Abra and Ilocos Sur provinces within Ilocos Region host the Bodong Indigenous Allied Group (BIAG), a codified customary-justice system with its own dispute-resolution authority over "crimes and tribal-related offences," recognised by Philippine courts. No trans-specific bodong ruling or customary exclusion was documented, but the legal-pluralism structure means that in a rural Abra or Ilocos Sur dispute, the applicable institution may not be a Philippine court.

Net effect: +0.03 above the national score, modest because the protective ordinance is municipal and the plural-justice uncertainty is localized to specific provinces within the region. Compare Central Visayas (0.63), where the ordinance cluster is broader (city IRRs with UNDP backing, unanimous municipal votes) and there is no countervailing alternative-justice structure.
